deck.title: Service Catalog & Trusted Advisor
deck.analogy: Service Catalog is a vending machine of pre-approved infrastructure; Trusted Advisor is an automated AWS consultant that audits your account.

cards.front: What is AWS Service Catalog?

back.answer: A vending machine of pre-approved infrastructure: admins define products and group them into portfolios; users launch them self-service.
back.explanation: Products are CloudFormation templates. Users get compliant stacks without keys to the kitchen.

cards.front: In Service Catalog, what are products and portfolios?

back.answer: Products are CloudFormation templates; portfolios are groups of products shared with users or accounts.

cards.front: How can Service Catalog users launch stacks without broad IAM permissions?

back.answer: Service Catalog launches on their behalf using its own constrained role.
back.explanation: A data scientist can launch the approved EMR cluster without permission to create EMR clusters directly.

cards.front: Which service fits "allow teams to deploy only approved, standardized, compliant configurations via self-service"?

back.answer: Service Catalog

cards.front: What is AWS Trusted Advisor?

back.answer: An automated AWS consultant that continuously scans your account and flags best-practice issues.

cards.front: Trusted Advisor Cost Optimization pillar: example checks?

back.answer: Idle EC2 instances, unattached Elastic IPs, underused RDS.

cards.front: Trusted Advisor Performance pillar: example checks?

back.answer: Overutilized instances and high-latency configurations.

cards.front: Trusted Advisor Security pillar: example checks?

back.answer: Security groups open to 0.0.0.0/0, MFA missing on root, public S3 buckets.

cards.front: Trusted Advisor Fault Tolerance pillar: example checks?

back.answer: Missing Multi-AZ, snapshots not taken, single-AZ exposure.

cards.front: Trusted Advisor Service Limits pillar: what does it check?

back.answer: Whether you're approaching a service quota, e.g. near your VPC or EC2 limit.

cards.front: Trusted Advisor: a team can't see Cost Optimization checks. Why?

back.answer: Their support plan: full checks, including all Cost Optimization, need Business or Enterprise support.
back.explanation: Free tier gives only core checks (basic security + service limits). It's not a permissions problem.

cards.front: Does Trusted Advisor fix issues it finds? How to alert?

back.answer: No, it only recommends; pair it with EventBridge/CloudWatch for alerts on check status changes.

cards.front: Config vs Inspector vs Trusted Advisor: what does each answer?

back.answer: Config: is a resource compliant with my rules? Inspector: software vulnerabilities on workloads. Trusted Advisor: broad best-practice checks across five pillars.

cards.front: Non-technical teams must deploy infrastructure, but only pre-approved configurations, without broad IAM permissions. Which service?

back.answer: Service Catalog

choices.why: Approved products launched on users' behalf.

cards.front: Identify idle instances and unattached Elastic IPs to reduce the bill. Which service?

back.answer: Trusted Advisor (Cost Optimization pillar)

choices.why: Provisions approved stacks, doesn't audit cost.
Cost Optimization checks find idle resources.
Checks rule compliance, not idle cost.

cards.front: A team sees only a few Trusted Advisor checks. Why?

back.answer: Support plan: full checks need Business/Enterprise.

choices.why: Free tier has only core checks.

cards.front: Get warned before hitting an AWS service quota. Which feature?

back.answer: Trusted Advisor Service Limits check

cards.front: Flag security groups allowing unrestricted access and missing root MFA. Which service?

back.answer: Trusted Advisor (Security pillar)

choices.why: Security checks cover open SGs and root MFA.

cards.front: Central IT curates standard CloudFormation-based products for business units. Which service?

back.answer: Service Catalog portfolios
back.explanation: Products live in portfolios, shared to users/accounts.

back.answer: Service Catalog
